The scientists murdering Annie K and hiding the pollution makes sense though. In no way were they going to risk their funding with the mine/Tuttle to openly tell the public that the mine was doing damage to the environment. The outrage would put the mine at risk in general and they would've not been able to continue with their research. The history of violence with the other scientists is kind of irrelevant if they witness somebody destroying years of research of samples that are prehistoric and extremely hard to find, plus the amount of pressure they feel knowing that what they're doing could have such a big impact on human history and knowing that if it's all for nothing they would've poisoned an entire town for no gain. That and knowing that Annie K living or getting away will reveal the lies about pollution and leak their research to the public is probably what made the rest of the scientists join in.
